newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich makes storming stock market debut.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich makes storming stock market debut.

text.p: Former building society Woolwich Plc stormed onto the London stock market on Monday, its shares opening at 368 pence each, significantly higher than pre-flotation predictions of around 320 pence.

The market's enthusiastic response to the bank's debut means shareholders -- people who were savers or borrowers with Woolwich when it was mutually owned -- would receive an average windfall of shares worth 2,418 pounds ($4,080) at the opening level.

The shares had slipped back to 349 pence at 0853 GMT, in line with general weakness among bank stocks. But even at this level Woolwich's market capitalisation is 5.58 billion pounds ($9.4 billion), making it one of Britain's top-10 banks and one of the biggest companies quoted on the exchange.

Around 2.5 million people who were members of the former building society, which was founded in 1847 in London, will receive at least 450 free shares. Someone with the maximum allowance, as both saver and borrower, will get 2,900 shares.
Dealers said the high early price in the shares was the result of a lack of stock and takeover speculation, predicting the price would fall back by the end of the first day's trading.
Around 23.1 percent of the shares are due to be sold at auction to institutional investors over the next few days, with those who have chosen to sell receiving an average price from the sales.

Woolwich is the latest building society to demutualise and seek the freedom of the stock exchange flotation, following the path trailed by Alliance & Leicester Plc and Halifax Plc in recent months. It will soon be joined by Northern Rock. ($ = 0.591 British Pounds)
